quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: All the time, no matter the weather.
Only if you will ride for more than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: All the time, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding. It protects you against the sun and skin injuries, even in warm weather.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is safe as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
Can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may lose control and drift into another lane or off the road. Always slow down for turns.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: Your feet can touch the ground when you are seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet can touch the ground when you are seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while seated. You should also be able to reach all controls easily.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Limits your movement in your lane.
Lets you depend on other drivers to watch for hazards.
Means you must ride faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react safely if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only if it is cloudy.
Use your headlight if you choose to.

questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane so they can share it.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. If you can do so safely, change lanes. Speeding up will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, the operator should:

options.text: Keep a longer distance from other vehicles.
Let air out of the tires for the extra weight.
Not warn the passenger about hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. Keep more space between you and other vehicles for safety.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for riders.

questions.question: Motorcycles must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must have headlights, taillights, brake lights, reflectors, brakes, turn signals, mirrors, fenders, footrests, a horn, and a muffler. A flag is not required.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be prevented by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best defense in an accident.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off other vehicles.
The one that allows other drivers to see you.
The one that places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that allows other drivers to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you. This helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good lane position keeps other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you space to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should motorcycle riders watch for?

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.

questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. Cars may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces suddenly.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do with your feet?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as this may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can use them quickly if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs tell you the rules you must follow on the road.

questions.question: When downshifting, what should you do?

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way down to neutral first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, go down one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly between each downshift.

questions.question: When braking, which brake should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time to stop. They work best when used together.

questions.question: How can your body get rid of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: What type of shoe soles should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Wear riding boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with soles that are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed to get other drivers' attention.

questions.question: How can you lower your crash risk?

options.text: Tell other drivers your plans using signals and position.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in parts of the lane where others cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers your plans using signals and position.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by being visible to others. Use turn signals and position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and next to you.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to see if it looks flat.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine even when it is under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: What does smooth downshifting on a motorcycle do?

options.text: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
You should not do it when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Engine braking from smooth downshifting is helpful. When you use engine braking, activate your brake lights so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Always reduce your speed on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: When should you completely check your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle completely before every ride. Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars.
